title: Indian History Test 1 (Ancient & Medieval — most probable)

questions.q: The Great Bath, a famous structure of the Indus Valley Civilisation, was found at:
questions.explain: The Great Bath was a large water tank at Mohenjo-daro, on the Indus river in present-day Sindh.

questions.q: The city of Harappa was situated on the bank of which river?
questions.explain: Harappa stood on the Ravi; Mohenjo-daro stood on the Indus — this pair is asked again and again.

questions.q: Lothal, the Indus Valley site in Gujarat, is famous for its:
questions.explain: Lothal had an artificial dockyard, showing the Harappans traded by sea.

questions.q: Dholavira, the Harappan city in the Rann of Kutch, is best known for its:
questions.explain: Dholavira's reservoirs and water channels show remarkable water harvesting in a dry region.

questions.q: Which is the oldest of the four Vedas?
questions.explain: The Rigveda is the earliest Veda; its hymns are the oldest religious texts of India.

questions.q: The national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from:
questions.explain: It is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad and appears below the national emblem.

questions.q: Gautam Buddha was born at:
questions.explain: Buddha was born at Lumbini (Nepal); Bodh Gaya = enlightenment, Sarnath = first sermon, Kushinagar = death.

questions.q: Buddha attained enlightenment at:
questions.explain: Under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya, Bihar, Siddhartha became the Buddha (the Enlightened One).

questions.q: Buddha gave his first sermon at:
questions.explain: At Sarnath near Varanasi he preached the first sermon, called Dharmachakra Pravartana (turning of the wheel of dharma).

questions.q: Buddha's Mahaparinirvana (death) took place at:
questions.explain: Kushinagar in Uttar Pradesh is where Buddha passed away; the four Buddhist sites form a favourite set of four.

questions.q: Mahavira, the Jain teacher who reorganised Jainism, was the:
questions.explain: Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara; the first was Rishabhanatha.

questions.q: Who was the first Tirthankara of Jainism?
questions.explain: Rishabhanatha (Adinath) is regarded as the first of the 24 Jain Tirthankaras.

questions.q: The Mauryan Empire was founded by:
questions.explain: Chandragupta founded the empire around 322 Before Common Era (BCE) with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya).

questions.q: The famous treatise 'Arthashastra' on statecraft was written by:
questions.explain: Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya's minister, wrote the Arthashastra on administration and economics.

questions.q: The Kalinga War, which changed Ashoka's life, was fought in about:
questions.explain: After the bloodshed of Kalinga (261 Before Common Era (BCE)), Ashoka gave up war and adopted Buddhism and the policy of Dhamma.

questions.q: Most of Ashoka's edicts were written in which language?
questions.explain: Ashoka addressed common people in their own language, Prakrit, across most of his empire.

questions.q: Most Ashokan edicts are written in which script?
questions.explain: Brahmi was the main script; Kharoshthi was used only in the north-west of his empire.

questions.q: Ashoka's Brahmi inscriptions were first deciphered by:
questions.explain: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837, which revealed the identity of King Ashoka.

questions.q: India's national emblem, the Lion Capital, was originally installed at:
questions.explain: Ashoka erected the Lion Capital pillar at Sarnath; it was adopted as the national emblem on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: The Kushan ruler most associated with patronising Mahayana Buddhism was:
questions.explain: Kanishka convened the Fourth Buddhist Council and spread Mahayana Buddhism to Central Asia.

questions.q: The Gupta period is popularly called the:
questions.explain: Science, literature and art flourished under the Guptas, so the period is called India's Golden Age.

questions.q: The great astronomer-mathematician Aryabhata belonged to the period of the:
questions.explain: Aryabhata (5th century Common Era (CE)) wrote the Aryabhatiya during the Gupta age.

questions.q: 'Abhijnana Shakuntalam', the famous Sanskrit play, was written by:
questions.explain: Kalidasa, the greatest Sanskrit poet-dramatist, adorned the Gupta court.

questions.q: The Gupta ruler who took the title 'Vikramaditya' was:
questions.explain: Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) defeated the Shakas and extended the Gupta empire to the west coast.

questions.q: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of:
questions.explain: Fa-Hien came in the early 5th century Common Era (CE) and described the prosperous Gupta rule.

questions.q: Which Gupta ruler is called the 'Napoleon of India' by historian V.A. Smith?
questions.explain: Samudragupta earned the title for his extensive military conquests across India.

questions.q: The Delhi Sultanate was established in 1206 by:
questions.explain: Aibak, a former slave-general of Muhammad Ghori, founded the Sultanate and the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty.

questions.q: The construction of the Qutub Minar at Delhi was begun by:
questions.explain: Aibak started the Qutub Minar; Iltutmish completed most of it later.

questions.q: Alauddin Khilji is best remembered in exams for his:
questions.explain: Alauddin fixed prices of essential goods and controlled markets to maintain a large army cheaply.

questions.q: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to:
questions.explain: His shift of capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri) failed and caused great hardship — a favourite exam experiment.

questions.q: The Tughlaq ruler who introduced token currency was:
questions.explain: His brass/copper token coins failed because people forged them freely at home.

questions.q: The first woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was:
questions.explain: Razia, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1240 — the Sultanate's only woman ruler.

questions.q: Krishnadevaraya, the greatest ruler of Vijayanagara, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explain: Krishnadevaraya of the Tuluva dynasty made Vijayanagara the dominant power of South India.

questions.q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
questions.explain: Babur defeated the Delhi Sultan Ibrahim Lodi and founded the Mughal Empire.

questions.q: Babur's victory at Panipat in 1526 is linked with his use of:
questions.explain: Babur's guns and tulughma tactics outclassed Lodi's much larger army.

questions.q: The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar's forces and:
questions.explain: Akbar's guardian Bairam Khan defeated Hemu, securing Mughal rule in north India.

questions.q: Which Mughal emperor abolished the jizya tax on non-Muslims?
questions.explain: Akbar abolished jizya as part of his policy of religious tolerance (sulh-i-kul); Aurangzeb later reimposed it.

questions.q: The new religious order 'Din-i-Ilahi' was started by:
questions.explain: Akbar proclaimed Din-i-Ilahi in 1582, blending elements of several religions.

questions.q: Fatehpur Sikri, the city built as his capital, was founded by:
questions.explain: Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri near Agra and shifted his capital there for some years.

questions.q: The Mansabdari system of ranking officers was introduced by:
questions.explain: Under Mansabdari, every officer held a rank (mansab) fixing his pay and the troops he maintained.
